pr.title: Re-enable the early otherwise branch optimization
pr.description:
Closes #95162. Fixes #119014.

This is the first part of #121397.

An invalid enum discriminant can come from anywhere. We have to check to see if all successors contain the discriminant statement. This should have a pass to hoist instructions.

r? cjgillot
pr.author: dianqk

issues.title: Early otherwise branch MIR opt is unsound
Unnecesary discriminant checks in `PartialEq`/`PartialOrd` style code on enums
issues.body:
I tried this code: [compiler explorer](https://godbolt.org/z/4hnGhPshW) ```rust pub enum Enum { A(u32), B(u32), C(u32), } #[no_mangle] pub fn f1(lhs: &Enum, rhs: &Enum) -> bool { match (lhs, rhs) { (Enum::A(lhs), Enum::A(rhs)) => lhs == rhs, (Enum::B(lhs), Enum::B(rhs)) => lhs == rhs, (Enum::C(lhs), Enum::C(rhs)) => lhs == rhs, _ => false, } } #[no_mangle] pub fn f2(lhs: &Enum, rhs: &Enum) -> bool { if std::mem::discriminant(lhs) != std::mem::discriminant(rhs) { return false; } match (lhs, rhs) { (Enum::A(lhs), Enum::A(rhs)) => lhs == rhs, (Enum::B(lhs), Enum::B(rhs)) => lhs == rhs, (Enum::C(lhs), Enum::C(rhs)) => lhs == rhs, _ => false, } } #[no_mangle] pub fn f3(lhs: &Enum, rhs: &Enum) -> bool { if std::mem::discriminant(lhs) != std::mem::discriminant(rhs) { return false; } match (lhs, rhs) { (Enum::A(lhs), Enum::A(rhs)) => lhs == rhs, (Enum::B(lhs), Enum::B(rhs)) => lhs == rhs, (Enum::C(lhs), Enum::C(rhs)) => lhs == rhs, _ => unsafe { std::hint::unreachable_unchecked() }, } } ``` Code like this is often used for implementations of `PartialEq` or `PartialOrd` on enums, so it is important that it be optimized well. I expected to see this happen: The functions `f1` and `f2` should produce equivalent machine code to `f3`. Instead, this happened: `f1` and `f2` do not produce equivalent machine code. `f1` is missing the early return for when the discriminants do not match. `f2` unnecessarily examines the discriminant of `lhs` twice! LLVM should be able to transform `f1` into `f2`, and `f2` into `f3` ### Meta `rustc --version --verbose`: ``` rustc 1.76.0-nightly (a96d57bdb 2023-12-15) binary: rustc commit-hash: a96d57bdb6d2bb6d233d7d5aaefc2995ab99be01 commit-date: 2023-12-15 host: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu release: 1.76.0-nightly LLVM version: 17.0.6 ```

analysis.summary: Fixes unsound hoisting in EarlyOtherwiseBranch by only optimizing when the parent switch's otherwise successor is an empty unreachable block, removing the projection-based may_hoist test, and preserving the parent otherwise target on the newly created equal-variant switch. The pass is re-enabled at MIR opt level 2. Tests use UnreachableEnumBranching to expose candidates.
analysis.originalLogic: EarlyOtherwiseBranch recognizes a parent `SwitchInt` on `discriminant(P)` whose case blocks contain child `SwitchInt`es on `discriminant(Q)` with matching equal-variant targets. It replaces repeated child discriminant switches with one hoisted child discriminant, an `Ne` comparison, and a single switch over the parent discriminant for the equal variants. Before this fix it ran only at `mir_opt_level() >= 3 && sess.opts.unstable_opts.unsound_mir_opts`, and `evaluate_candidate` allowed a reachable parent `otherwise`; `may_hoist` filtered only projection kinds such as Deref-of-reference, Field, and rejected Downcast/index. The old destination was `parent_dest.unwrap_or(child_targets.otherwise())`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical transformation hoisted `discriminant(Q)` before the parent switch even when the parent `otherwise` successor was a real block. This can compute a discriminant on a path where `Q` is uninitialized or holds an invalid enum value, for example after unsafe code writes a bad bit pattern on another parent arm. A projection filter like `may_hoist` does not prove that every reachable successor computes the child discriminant, and computing a discriminant of an invalid enum value is UB. A related destination error used `opt_data.destination`/the child fallback as the new equal-switch `otherwise`, which could turn an unlisted/invalid parent discriminant into a defined fallback instead of preserving the parent's unreachable/UB successor.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR functions containing tuple/struct matches over two or more enum places, where a parent discriminant switch has per-variant child discriminant switches. Relevant inputs include reachable parent `otherwise` paths, parent cases that bypass child discriminant computation, and unsafe/FFI-created invalid enum values. The valid optimization domain is a parent switch whose `otherwise` is empty+Unreachable and whose parent target branches all verify as child discriminant switches, so the child discriminant is computed on every reachable parent path. Tests cover `Option`/custom `Option2` enums, 2- and 3-element tuples, references, downcasts, and pointer dereferences.
analysis.trigger: A parent `SwitchInt` over `discriminant(P)` with an `otherwise` branch, at least one child case block beginning with `SwitchInt` over `discriminant(Q)`, and matching value targets. The pass should fire only after `bbs[targets.otherwise()].is_empty_unreachable()` succeeds and each parent target branch passes `verify_candidate_branch` as a child discriminant switch; it then inserts the hoisted child discriminant, `Ne`, and a new switch. Tests additionally use UnreachableEnumBranching so the parent `otherwise` becomes unreachable and the candidate is exposed.
preconditions: Parent switch otherwise must satisfy `bbs[targets.otherwise()].is_empty_unreachable()`: no statements and an Unreachable terminator.
Every reachable parent successor must contain the child discriminant computation; projection filtering alone is not a soundness argument.
All parent targets must verify as child discriminant switches over the same child place with expected value mapping; a parent case that directly reaches fallback must prevent optimization.
The newly created equal-value switch must use `parent_targets.otherwise()`, not the child fallback, so unlisted parent discriminants remain unreachable/UB.
Tests may require `-Zmir-enable-passes=+UnreachableEnumBranching` to turn the parent otherwise into an unreachable block before EarlyOtherwiseBranch runs.
pitfalls: Hoisting `discriminant(Q)` can evaluate an uninitialized or invalid enum value when another path mutates Q to an invalid bit pattern; an invalid discriminant computation is UB.
Allowing Deref-of-reference and Field projections via `may_hoist` does not prove the enum is valid or that the discriminant is computed in all branches.
Downcast validity may depend on the parent branch, but checking projection kinds alone is not a general proof of hoist safety.

Using `opt_data.destination` or `child_targets.otherwise()` as the equal-switch otherwise can route invalid/unlisted parent discriminants to fallback instead of the parent unreachable block, changing UB into defined behavior.
Do not conflate unsafe invalid-value creation with ordinary borrow-checker restrictions; the key test is validity/initialization of the hoisted place at the hoist point.
After UnreachableEnumBranching, `otherwise` may be unreachable while some parent targets still bypass the child discriminant switch; branch verification is still required.
analysis.testStrategy: Use mir-opt unit tests tagged `//@ unit-test: EarlyOtherwiseBranch` with `//@ compile-flags: -Zmir-enable-passes=+UnreachableEnumBranching`. Positive tests should FileCheck for a hoisted child `discriminant`, an `Ne` between parent and child discriminants, and a `switchInt` on the comparison, e.g. `[[CMP_LOCAL]] = Ne([[LOCAL1]], move [[LOCAL2]])` followed by `switchInt(move [[CMP_LOCAL]])`. Negative tests should FileCheck that after the parent discriminant there is no `Ne` and no second `discriminant` before the switch; the added `opt1` case is explicitly commented `// We can't optimize it because y may be an invalid value.` Include existing `no_downcast` and `no_deref_ptr` cases as soundness negatives. Inspect MIR diffs to verify the new equal-switch otherwise targets the original parent unreachable block (e.g. `otherwise: bb9` where `bb9: unreachable`), not the fallback. Add a codegen test for a full-enum match expecting an LLVM `select` with no `switch`/`br`.
evidence: An invalid enum discriminant can come from anywhere. We have to check to see if all successors contain the discriminant statement. This should have a pass to hoist instructions.
